name: Mental Game Framework
description: A study companion to Champions Stay Present, organized around the different questions before, during and after competition.
summary: Locate preparation, competition-day focus and performance review in Josh McKinney’s mindset syllabus.
overview: Being disappointed by a result and identifying a moment you lost focus are different review problems. Josh McKinney’s Champions Stay Present separates goal setting and camp preparation from competition day and post-event analysis. Use that structure to choose the part of the course that matches the experience you want to examine.

fits: Your competition notes record results but say little about what held your attention during the match.
consider_alternative_if: If the immediate problem is travel, packing or coach arrangements, Competition Preparation System has a more practical logistics focus.

includes: Six volumes covering the method, goals and camp, over-training, champions’ perspectives, competition day and post-competition analysis.
Separate places to study event-day focus and retrospective review.
limits: The public outline identifies topics without explaining the course’s mental exercises.
This companion focuses on competition reflection; it does not supply psychological treatment or a conditioning plan.

start_here.title: Separate attention during the match from hindsight
start_here.task: Choose one competition you remember clearly. In one column record what occupied your attention before and during the match; in another record what you concluded after seeing the result. Identify a mismatch you want to investigate. The outline places event-day material in Volume 5 and retrospective analysis in Volume 6; owners can compare those two lessons against that specific example.
start_here.section: Volume 5: Compete Like you train: Navigating Competition Day. Volume 6: Let’s do that again: Post Competition Analysis.
